key_insight: Careful 3D-specific data augmentation and removing Batch Normalization unlock stable training of powerful 3D perception models for policy learning; coupling a transformer-based 3D encoder with a diffusion decoder yields robust, generalizable 3D policies.
problem_solved: Addresses training instability and severe overfitting in 3D policy learning that prevented using scalable 3D perception backbones and limited generalization/cross-embodiment transfer.
method: Systematic diagnosis of failure modes, identifying missing 3D data augmentation and harmful effects of Batch Normalization as primary causes.
Introduce 3D-aware augmentation pipelines and mitigate BatchNorm-related instabilities (replace/modify normalization strategy to suit small-batch 3D RL).
Design a scalable pipeline: transformer-based 3D encoder paired with a diffusion-model decoder to produce stable, generalizable policies.
impact: Enables reliable training of large 3D perception models for control, improving generalization and cross-embodiment transfer in robotics and simulated agents; reduces the barrier to adopt modern 3D architectures in policy learning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: 3D input → transformer encoder → diffusion decoder → policy output
Before/After chart: training stability and overfitting metrics with vs. without 3D augmentation & BatchNorm fixes
Illustration of 3D augmentation examples (rotations, occlusions, noise) applied to point clouds/voxels
Iconic flow showing improved cross-embodiment transfer (same policy deployed on different robot silhouettes)
paper_authors: Zhengdong Hong, Shenrui Wu, Haozhe Cui, Boyi Zhao, Ran Ji
